Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Young adult female with progressive numbness, tingling, and weakness of the left arm, specifically involving second, third, and fourth fingers on the palmar side, with associated fine motor difficulty (piano playing)  
- Recent episode of transient monocular visual field loss in left eye lasting approximately 20 minutes, consistent with possible optic neuritis  
- Recent viral illness approximately 4 weeks ago preceding neurological symptoms  
- Family history includes autoimmune disease (father) and metabolic conditions (mother)  
- Differential diagnosis:  
  • Multiple sclerosis (MS) – High likelihood due to constellation of transient visual symptoms, progressive unilateral limb sensory and motor symptoms, recent viral illness, and family history of autoimmune disease  
  • Transient ischemic attack (TIA)/stroke – Moderate likelihood given transient vision loss and unilateral symptoms but less consistent with progressive worsening and absence of vascular risk factors  
  • Cervical radiculopathy/nerve injury from boxing – Moderate likelihood given recent boxing activity and hand symptoms but visual symptoms unexplained by peripheral nerve injury alone  
  • Post-viral inflammatory neuropathy – Moderate likelihood; symptom onset after viral illness supports this, but unilateral plus visual symptoms favor CNS pathology  
  • Cervical spinal cord tumor – Low likelihood; progressive unilateral symptoms possible but visual symptoms and absence of neck pain make less likely  
- No contradictions noted between transcript and DDx  

Management Plan  
- Urgent neurology referral for further assessment including brain imaging (MRI) to evaluate for demyelinating disease or other CNS pathology  
- No acute medications initiated; steroids or specific treatment to be considered after diagnosis confirmation  
- Patient advised to seek emergency care if symptoms worsen (e.g., spread of weakness, worsening vision, headaches, vomiting, seizures)  
- Continue symptomatic management with occasional ibuprofen for pain; vitamin D and melatonin as before  
- Discuss compliance with iron supplementation during follow-up

- Transient ischemic attack (TIA)/stroke – Moderate likelihood: Supported by transient visual field loss and unilateral arm symptoms; less likely due to progressive symptoms and absence of vascular risk factors.  
- Cervical radiculopathy/nerve injury due to boxing – Moderate likelihood: Consistent with boxing activity and focal arm symptoms; visual symptoms not explained by this diagnosis alone.
